description: What makes a witness-lane message conformant, as an ordered predicate chain. A rejection attestation's R resolves here: its I is the subject's derivations only (topic, consensus timestamp, sequence, byte-hash - never the payload, W-10), its O is the verdict plus reason codes from the closed space. Success bears no verdict: a stamp that passes every predicate IS its own verdict (D-6/D-7), and this rule authorizes rendering failures only.

inputsSpec.subjectTopicId: the lane topic the attempt landed on
inputsSpec.subjectSequenceNumber: the attempt's sequence number on that topic
inputsSpec.subjectMessageHash: keccak256 of the attempt's raw message bytes - the only derivation an invalid message gets

predicates.check: the raw bytes parse as JSON
the payload declares a schema field
the declared schema is a recognized witness schema (hcs.ontologic.witness.stamp or hcs.ontologic.morphemeProof)
the proof carries ruleId, ruleUri, ruleUriHash, inputsHash, outputsHash, bindingHash as non-empty strings
ruleUriHash, inputsHash, outputsHash, bindingHash are 32-byte hex
Peirce: bindingHash recomputes as keccak256(canonical({ruleUri, inputsHash, outputsHash}))
the split holds: ruleUriHash equals sha256 of the ruleUri string
Floridi: the ruleUri dereferences to a self-verifying RuleDef in its registry

verdictClause.success: no verdict is rendered - the stamp is the verdict; nothing exists for this rule to add
verdictClause.failure: verdict 'rejected' with the failing predicate's ReasonCode; reasons never carry subject-message content - a reason that must point at something points with a hash or an offset, never a value (W-10)

reasonSpaceRef: packages/core/src/reasons.ts REASONS - codes are the wire format; display templates are renderer-side only
